subject.title: fix(reef): keep routine agent replies from disappearing

question: Should Reef's outbound DLP permanently default-allow non-secret code, logs, hostnames, configuration, and internal identifiers, or should plausibly confidential/internal material remain review-gated?
rationale: This changes Reef's documented fail-closed trust boundary rather than only correcting a classifier false positive, so repository policy and tests cannot determine the intended confidentiality posture.

options.title: Keep internal material review-gated
options.body: Allow ordinary coordination but route plausibly confidential code, logs, hostnames, configuration, and identifiers to owner review unless clearly public or non-sensitive.

options.title: Approve broader default allow
options.body: Adopt the proposed policy explicitly and require live leak-resistance evidence plus documentation of the narrower DLP guarantee.

recommendation.title: Keep internal material review-gated
recommendation.body: Allow ordinary coordination but route plausibly confidential code, logs, hostnames, configuration, and identifiers to owner review unless clearly public or non-sensitive.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is self-assigned and maintainer-labeled, and this person owns the complete branch-level Reef policy and recovery design.
